title: The Old Neighbourhood (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 98bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist Perth Zimbabwe memory nostalgia
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The old neighbourhood is still there but it's not the same old neighbourhood
The houses are the same addresses but they're changed in the understood
Way that places change when you're not there to notice the degrees
The old neighbourhood grew up without me — naturally

[Pre-Chorus]
I drove through the first street I ever knew at forty-three
And the tree I'd climbed was still there and it recognised me

[Chorus]
The old neighbourhood knows something I don't know
It knows that everyone who left kept leaving in the grow
The old neighbourhood has new people in all the old positions
And they're making the same discoveries in the same first-year conditions
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The corner shop is now something different and the school has been extended
And the park where we played cricket has been aesthetically amended
But the gradient of the street is the same and the way the light falls
In the afternoon is unchanged — the old neighbourhood calls

[Bridge]
In Zimbabwe the street I grew up on is still the same width
And the tree outside the house is thirty years taller — not a myth
And the gate that I walked through every morning of my childhood
Still opens outward and that is the detail that I understood

[Outro]
Old neighbourhood knows where you've been… and where you're going…
The gardens still growing
